GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
 DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS  
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2224 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 31.07.2026 
 
PM PRANAM Scheme 
 
2224. Shri Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu: 
Shri Putta Mahesh Kumar: 
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) the total amount of funds sanctioned and released to the states under the PM 
Programme for Restoration, Awareness Generation, Nourishment, and Amelioration of 
Mother Earth (PM PRANAM) scheme since inception, State-wise and year-wise;  
(b)  the area and farmers covered under the scheme, State-wise and district-wise for 
Andhra Pradesh;  
(c)  the financial assistance released to farmers, State-wise and district-wise for Andhra 
Pradesh indicating the timeline by which the first incentive under the scheme is planned 
to be disbursed;  
(d) whether there are issues in incentive disbursal, if so, the details thereof;  
(e)  whether the Government plans to continue the said scheme during the financial year 
2025–26, if so, the details of the proposed extension and budgetary allocations; and  
(f)  the total quantity of chemical fertilisers, Urea, DAP, NPK, MOP consumed during the 
last five years, year-wise and State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
 (SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
 (a) to (e) The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), on June 28, 2023, 
approved the “PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness Generation, Nourishment, and 
Amelioration of Mother-Earth (PM-PRANAM)” for the period from 2023-24 to 2025-26. This 
initiative aims to support the mass movement initiated by States and Union Territories (UTs) 
to preserve the health of Mother Earth through the promotion of sustainable and balanced 
fertilizer use, adoption of alternative fertilizers, promotion of organic farming, and 
implementation of resource conservation technologies.  
All States/UTs are covered under the PM-PRANAM scheme, including the State of 
Andhra Pradesh. The incentives to States/UTs for reduction of consumption of chemical 
fertilizers (Urea, DAP, NPK, MOP) in a given financial year, compared to the average 
consumption over the previous three years, under the Scheme is equivalent to 50% of the 
fertilizer subsidy saved by the State. The incentives can be utilized for promotional activities 
(IEC) & R&D relating to agricultural infrastructure and increase in the yield. The remaining 50% 
of the subsidy is retained by Govt. of India. 

The incentives to States/UTs for reduction of consumption of chemical fertilizers (Urea, 
DAP, NPK, MOP) has not yet been disbursed.  
(f) The State-wise details regarding the sales of Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS during the 
last five years are placed at Annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2225
TO BE ANSWERED ON 31ST JULY2026
FINANCIAL ASSISTANCES UNDER NHM
†2225. DR. RAJESH MISHRA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the annual financial assistance provided to the States under National Health Mission
(NHM) for the operation and maintenance of 108 Emergency Response Services and Janani Express
vehicles;
(b) whether the Government is aware that the ambulance response in Sidhi District is considerably
high and that, pregnant women and critically ill patients often fail to reach hospitals in time due to
the breakdown of vehicles, if so, the details thereof;
(c) the total number of new ambulances and Advanced Life Support (ALS) ambulances sanctioned
for the Parliamentary constituency during the last two years;
(d) the total number of such vehicles functioning properly in the district; and
(e) whether the payments due to the agencies providing these services are being made on time, if so,
the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a): “Public Health” and “Hospital” are state subject, the primary responsibility for strengthening
public healthcare system, including adequately equipped ambulances, especially for emergency care
network, lies with the respective State/UT Governments.
However, under National Health Mission (NHM), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
provides the technical and financial support to the States/UTs as per the proposals submitted by
them in the form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) based on the requirements,
including the provision for Dial 108, Dial 102/104, Basic Life Support (BLS) and Advance Life
Support (ALS) ambulances, and the approvals are accorded as Record of Proceedings (RoP) to
States/UTs. Dial 108 is predominantly an emergency response system, primarily designed to
attend to patients of critical care, trauma and accident victims etc. The RoPs can be accessed at
https://nhm.gov.in/index1.php?lang=1&level=1&sublinkid=1377&lid=744.
(b) to (e): As per the information provided by the State Government of Madhya Pradesh, in
District Sidhi, the average response time for the 108 Ambulance service is 19 minutes and 51

seconds in rural areas and 18 minutes and 17 seconds in urban sectors. Similarly, the Janani
clocks an average response time of 15 minutes and 33 seconds in rural areas and 13 minutes and
50 seconds in urban sectors. These operational timelines are in accordance with the service
delivery standards prescribed by the Government of India (NAS).
As informed by the State, no new Basic Life Support (BLS) or Advanced Life Support
(ALS) ambulances have been sanctioned in Sidhi parliamentary constituency over the last two
financial years. The district's existing fleet is fully operational with zero mechanical or logistical
disruptions. The active deployment includes 17 Basic Life Support (BLS) Ambulances, 03
Advanced Life Support (ALS) Ambulances and 19 Janani Express (Patient Transport Vehicles).
Further, the State has informed that there are no outstanding liabilities or pending vendor
payments at the state level. The State systematically executes all financial clearings immediately
upon receiving valid invoices.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2226
TO BE ANSWERED ON 31ST JULY2026
PREV ALENCEOF ANAEMIA AND MALNUTRITION IN WOMEN
†2226. SHRI RAJKUMAR ROAT:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the prevalence of anaemia and malnutrition among pregnant
women in tribal-dominated areas of Rajasthan is extremely severe and out of 10,175 pregnant
women screened in Dungarpur District during April, 2025 to February, 2026, approximately
7,000 were found to be anaemic;
(b) if so, the details of the cases of anaemic pregnant women in tribal-dominated areas during
the last five years, year-wise;
(c) whether it is a fact that out of 4,584 units of blood issued at the Dungarpur District
hospital
during the said period, 2,544 units had to be transfused to pregnant women, if so, the details
thereof and the reasons therefor along with the factors behind the situation despite the
ongoing
POSHAN Abhiyan and Iron-Folic Acid (IFA) programme;
(d) whether the Government proposes to implement a special action plan for the prevention of
anaemia and malnutrition among pregnant women in tribal-dominated districts; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (c) As per National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5, 2019-21), the prevalence of
anaemia among pregnant women is 46.3 percent and among Schedule Tribe women aged 15-
49 years is 61.6 percent in the State of Rajasthan. The prevalence of anaemia among all
women aged 15-49 years is 72.6 percent in the district Dungarpur and 54.4 percent in the
State of Rajasthan as per NFHS-5 (2019-21).

As per the information received from the State of Rajasthan, during April 2025 to February
2026, a total of 34,304 pregnant women were screened in Dungarpur district. Out of these,
3,152 women were found to have severe anaemia (Hb below 7 g/dl). During the same period,
5,390 units of blood and blood components were supplied by the Government Medical
College and Associated Hospital, Dungarpur. Out of these, 1,662 units were used for blood
transfusion to manage severe anaemia among pregnant women.
(d) and (e) As per information received from the State of Rajasthan, Pradhan Mantri
Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) is organized on the 9th, 18th and 27th of every month,
and Shakti Diwas every Tuesday, and Mother Child Health and Nutrition (MCHN) Day every
Thursday to improve maternal health.
The Government of India provides support to the States for the implementation of various
schemes/initiatives to improve maternal health outcomes among pregnant women across the
country, including the tribal-dominated districts, key amongst which are as follows:
 Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan: The Government of India has recently released
the Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan –Operational guidelines during the 16th Central
Council of Health and Family Welfare (CCHFW) meeting on 29th June 2026 to
address the high prevalence of anaemia through a 7X7X7 strategy, moving ahead
from the older 6X6X6 strategy of Anemia Mukt Bharat programme to reduce anemia
with focused attention among seven beneficiaries age groups through implementation
of seven interventions supported by seven institutional mechanisms.
The pregnant women are provided Prophylactic Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation;
Testing of anaemia at every ANC visit; Therapeutic management of anaemia (oral IFA
tablets, Intravenous Iron, Blood transfusion) as per anemia management protocols;
Deworming among second trimester, Jan Bhagidari- communication approach to
counteract normalised perception of anemia and improve compliance to IFA
supplementation; Eating Right strategy to promote consumption of locally available iron
rich food and diet diversification.
 Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) is a demand promotion and conditional cash
transfer scheme for promoting institutional delivery.
 Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) entitles all pregnant woman
delivering in public health institutions to have absolutely free and no expense
delivery, including caesarean section. The entitlements include free drugs,

consumables, free diet during stay, free diagnostics, free transportation and free blood
transfusion, if required. Similar entitlements are also in place for sick infants up to
one year of age.
 Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) provides pregnant
women a fixed day, free of cost, assured and quality antenatal check up by a
Specialist/Medical Officer on the 9th day of every month.
Extended PMSMA strategy ensures quality antenatal care (ANC) to pregnant women,
especially to high-risk pregnant (HRP) women and individual HRP tracking until a safe
delivery is achieved by means of financial incentivization for the identified high-risk
pregnant women and accompanying ASHA for extra 3 visits over and above
the PMSMA visit.
 Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan (SUMAN) provides assured, dignified, respectful
and quality healthcare at no cost and zero tolerance for denial of services for every
pregnant woman and newborn visiting public health facilities to end all preventable
maternal and newborn deaths.
 Optimizing Postnatal Care aims to strengthen the quality of post-natal care by
laying emphasis on detection of danger signs in mothers and incentivization of
Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs) for prompt detection, referral &
treatment of such high-risk postpartum mothers.
 Functionalization of First Referral Units (FRUs) by ensuring manpower, blood
storage units, referral linkages to improve the access to quality of care for pregnant
women
 Village Health Sanitation and Nutrition Days (VHSNDs) are observed for
provision of maternal and child health services and creating awareness on maternal
and child-care including nutrition in convergence with the Ministry of Women and
Child Development.
 Outreach camps are provisioned for improving the reach of health care services,
especially in tribal and hard-to-reach areas. This platform is used to increase
awareness for the Maternal & Child health services, community mobilization as well
as to track high-risk pregnancies.
 Birth Waiting Homes (BWH) are established in remote and tribal areas to promote
institutional delivery and improve access to healthcare facilities.

 Mother and Child Protection (MCP) Card and Safe Motherhood Booklet are
distributed to the pregnant women for educating them on diet, rest, danger signs of
pregnancy, benefit schemes and institutional deliveries.

Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the number of centres in the country that are fully operational with the expanded package of
comprehensive primary healthcare services under the Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs), State
-wise, especially in Rajasthan and the Dausa Parliamentary Constituency;
(b) the number of Sub-Health Centres and Primary Health Centres upgraded into AAMs in the
country, State-wise, particularly in Rajasthan and the Dausa Parliamentary Constituency since
the year 2022 to date;
(c) whether priority has been accorded to tribal and underprivileged areas in the establishment
and strengthening of these centres, particularly in the Dausa Parliamentary Constituency, if so,
the details thereof; and
(d) whether any special action plan is being implemented by the Government to enhance the
availability of doctors, healthcare workers, essential medicines, diagnostic facilities and digital
health services in the AAMs, if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (d): As reported by States/UTs on Ayushman Arogya Mandir (AAM) portal, a total of
1,86,298 AAMs including 31,347 AAMs in 178 tribal districts have been operationalized by
strengthening Sub-health Centres (SHCs) and Primary Health Centres (PHCs) in the country, as
on 30.06.2026. State/UT-wise number of AAMs operationalized across the country including
Rajasthan is enclosed as Annexure. As informed by State, 368 AAMs are operationalized in
Dausa Parliamentary Constituency of Rajasthan.
These AAMs incrementally provide 12 package of primary health care services across the country,
encompassing Reproductive and child care services, Communicable diseases, Non Communicable

2
diseases (NCD), Palliative Care and elderly Care, Care for common mental disorders, neurological
conditions (epilepsy,dementia) and substance use disorders management (tobacco, alcohol, drugs),
Oral health, ENT care, and Basic emergency care.
Resources available at all AAMs include building, human resource, essential drugs and diagnostics,
IT equipment and internet connectivity. For SHC-AAM, operational guidelines for AAMs provide
for, Community Health Officer (CHO), Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM) and Multipurpose
worker -Male along with ASHAs in the catchment area. For PHC-AAM, the norms provide for
Medical Officer, staff nurses, pharmacist, Health Assistants and Lab technician. Under Free Drugs
and Free Diagnostics Service Initiative, Government of India provides financial support to
States/UTs for 113 drugs & 14 diagnostic tests at SHC-AAM and 179 drugs & 63 tests at PHC-
AAM level.
The teleconsultation services, available at all operational AAMs across the country including
tribal and underprivileged areas, enables people to access the specialist services closer to their
homes addressing concerns of physical accessibility, shortage of service providers and to
facilitate continuum of care.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2229 TO BE ANSWERED ON 31.07.2026 
“Diversion of Fertilizers” 
2229. Shri Karti P Chidambaram: 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) the quantum of subsidized urea and DAP diverted for non-agricultural/industrial 
use as identified by enforcement agencies during the last two Kharif and Rabi 
seasons, State-wise; 
(b) the prosecutions launched, against dealers and companies found violating the 
Fertilizer Control Order, 1985; 
(c) whether Government has made any assessment regarding the adequacy of the 
neem-coating and point-of-sale verification mechanisms in preventing diversion, if so, 
the details thereof; and 
(d) the concrete steps proposed to prevent artificial shortages and price gouging 
ahead of the upcoming sowing season across the country, State-wise? 
 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) & (b) : In order to address the issues of black-marketing, hoarding, diversion of 
fertilizers and other malpractices, fertilizers are declared as an essential commodity 
under the Essential Commodities Act-1955 and notified under Fertilizer Control Order- 
1985. State Governments are adequately empowered to take action against persons 
involved in such malpractices, as per provisions of EC Act. The prosecutions launched, 
against dealers and companies found violating the Fertilizer Control Order, 1985. 
Moreover, Department of Agriculture & Farmer’s Welfare, in consultation with the State 
Governments, is regularly monitoring the enforcement action taken by States against 

the cases of Black marketing, Hoarding, Sub-standard and Diversion on weekly basis. 
As informed by DA&FW, in the country in FY 2025-26, 4,84,663 raids have been 
conducted, 17,392 show cause notices have been issued, 6,941 licenses have been 
suspended/cancelled, and 847 FIRs have been registered against defaulters. In FY 
2026-27 i.e. from 01.04.2026 to 24.07.2026, 1,69,031 raids have been conducted, 
9,127 show cause notices have been issued, 2,868 licenses have been 
suspended/cancelled and 270 FIRs have been registered against defaulters to curb 
these malpractices; the State-wise information of enforcement activities along with 
quantity of fertilizers seized in FY 2026-27 are placed at Annexure. 
 
(c):  During the year 2015, the Union Government made it mandatory for all the 
domestic producers and importers of Urea to supply 100% Neem Coated Urea. 
Subsequent to the introduction of Neem Coated Urea (NCU), one of the primary 
benefits of Neem Coating is that due to slow release, the consumption of NCU reduces 
as compared to normal urea. 
 
         Under DBT system for sale in Fertilizers, the sale of subsidized fertilizers is done 
by 100% Aadhaar based authentication of the beneficiary as per Section-7 of Aadhaar 
Act, 2016. Additionally, a monthly ceiling of 50 bags per buyer per month is placed for 
equitable distribution of fertilizers except for Telangana having the ceiling of 2 Bags 
per Acre (for Urea only) per buyer and Jammu & Kashmir having the ceiling of 60 bags 
per buyer per season. Based on the purchase, various reports are made available in 
the iFMS Dashboards for monitoring by respective State Officials. Additionally, under 
the ‘Framework for Fertilizer Sale’ in 42 identified districts of 21 States, the fertilizer is 
being sold to the identified farmer as per General Fertilizer Recommendation (GFR) 
based on land area and crop sown. Ceiling of bags is different in the Pilot districts 
under the ‘Framework for Fertilizer Sale’ as decided by the respective states. 
 
(d) :  Following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring timely 
and adequate availability of subsidized fertilizers in the country; 
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of 
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State 
Governments, assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. Based 

on requirement projected by DA & FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
(ii) The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout 
the country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
(iii) The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizer is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well in 
advance to ensure timely availability.  
(iv) The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with 
manufacturers and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of 
indents. 
(v) Regular coordination is done with the Ministry of Railways for giving 
sufficient rakes, priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
(vi) The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/block level is done 
by the concerned State government.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2231  
ANSWERED ON 31.07.2026  
  
BETI BACHAO, BETI PADHAO SCHEME IN PUNJAB  
  
2231. SHRI SUKHJINDER SINGH RANDHAWA:  
 
 Will the MINISTER OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:  
  
(a)  the details of the concrete steps taken under the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao scheme in Punjab 
to strengthen the lifecycle of the girl child, from birth through education, skill development 
and economic empowerment; and  
  
(b)  whether female foeticide, declining child sex ratio and disparity in girls' education continue 
to be matters of serious concern in certain districts of said State, if so, the details of the 
specific interventions undertaken therein district -wise? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) and (b) Beti Bachao Beti Padhao  helps to address Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and related issues of 
empowerment of girls and women. The scheme, launched on 22nd January 2015, as a collaborative 
effort between the Ministries of Women & Child Development, Education, and Health and Family 
Welfare, aims to prevent gender -biased sex selection, ensure the survival and protection of girl 
children, and promote their education.  
  
The scheme tries to create mindset and behavioural  changes towards the girl child by informing, 
influencing, motivating, engaging, and empowering various stakeholders. In the 15th Finance 
Commission Period, BBBP as a component under the SAMBAL vertical of Mission Shakti, has 
been expanded to cover all the  districts of the country through multi -sectoral interventions 
encouraging greater spend on activities that have impact on ground. BBBP has got transformed 
from a policy initiative into a national movement by mobilizing various stakeholders, including 
government agencies, media, civil society, and the public at large. BBBP primarily focuses on 
creating behavioural and social change in the way the girl child is perceived across the country.  

  
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is Centrally Sponsored Scheme and the Central Government provides 
100% financial assistance to States and UTs. The overall implementation of scheme lies with the 
State Governments and UT Administrations.  
  
As per the latest report of Health Management Information System (HMIS) of Ministry of  Health 
& Family Welfare (MoHFW ), Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB) at the national level has  increased from 
918 in 2014 -15 to 929 in 2025 -26 (provisional). Further, in the State of Punjab, the Sex Ratio at 
Birth (SRB) is showing improving trends and has increased from 892 to 922 during 2014 -15 to 
2025-26 (provisional).  
  
As per UDISE data of Ministry of Education, Gross enrolment ratio of girls in the schools at 
secondary level has increased from 75.51% in 2014 -15 to 83.4% in 2025 -26 at national level. 
Further, in the State of Punjab, Gross enrolment ratio of girls in the schools at secondary level has 
increased from 83.21% in 2014 -15 to 96.5% in 2025-26. 
  
Under the BBBP scheme, for effective implementation at ground level, Ministry has developed an 
operational manual which inter -alia includes a thematic calendar for suggested convergence 
activities including activities for raising awareness at district level with month wise specific themes 
for holistic development of the Girl Child and to ensure year -round engagement of girls, their 
families and communities and training in this regard is regularly conducted at district, state and 
national level. 
  
In the State of Punjab, awareness activities are being carried out at village, block and district level 
to sensitize the people against the declined Girl child Sex Ratio. Also, awareness activities are 
being conducted as per BBBP calendar issued by Ministr y of Women and Child Development, 
Government of India. In addition, to keep in mind the economic empowerment of women, special 
job camps for women are being held every year under BBBP in all 23 districts of Punjab, where, 
selection are done and appointment  letters are issued to the eligible women candidates on the spot 
by various companies. Further, free anaemia check-up camps for girl students are also organized 
in schools for early detection of anaemia  and to spread awareness among girl students related to 
health-related issues. Under the skill development initiatives, free driving, cooking, computer and 
stitching classes are provided to the needy girls in State of Punjab under the BBBP scheme to make 
them self -reliant and independent. Moreover, awareness activities are also carried out with the 
convergence of Department of Education, Health and Sports at district and block level in Punjab. 
Additionally, every year the festival of Lohri is celebrated at State and district level on the birth of 
girls in Punjab.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2232 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 31st JULY, 2026 
 
REPEAL OF OBSOLETE AND REDUNDANT LAWS 
2232. MS SAYANI GHOSH: 
 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of obsolete, redundant and outdated Central Acts and subordinate legislations 
repealed or amended by the Government since 2014, year-wise; 
 
(b) the details of the laws so repealed, including the Ministries/Departments to which they 
pertained, sector-wise; 
 
(c) the mechanism, committee or institutional framework adopted for identifying obsolete 
laws and the criteria followed for their repeal; 
 
 (d) whether the Government has assessed the impact of repealing such laws on ease of doing 
business, governance, judicial pendency and regulatory compliance, if so, the details thereof; 
and 
 
(e) whether any further review of existing laws is underway for repeal or simplification, if so, 
the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW 
AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a) to (e): On the basis of the Reports of the Law Commission  of India and the Two-member 
Committee constituted by the Government including the recommendations of various 
Ministries/Departments for repeal of laws administer ed by them, a total number of 1725 obsolete 
and redundant laws have been repealed by the Government since 2014 till date through various 
Repealing and Amending Acts  and other enactments. The details of the laws repealed during the 
said period are available on the official website of the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and 
Justice at 
https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/03/af8aae0b3bfc3e703fe57ae181e9d4ba.pdf 
for public access. 
 

2 
 
Repealing of obsolete legislations is an important commitment of the Government for 
achieving the larger objective of “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance”. The repeal of 
obsolete and redundant laws , besides reducing the volume of statute book, also reduces the 
compliance burden, thereby ensuring ease of living for citizens. It also provides clarity of existing 
laws to the executive, judiciary, stakeholders and the general public.  
 
The Legislative Department undertakes drafting of laws for repeal of obsolete and redundant 
laws administered by them on the basis of the policy decisions taken by the concerned 
administrative Ministries/Department and as per the procedure prescribed by the Ministry of 
Parliamentary Affairs in the Manual of Parliamentary Procedures. The Legislative Department has 
been taking necessary steps to ensure that legislative drafting is simple, plain, precise and 
unambiguous.  
 
Presently, the Twenty -third Law Commission of India, has also been  constituted vide 
notification dated 02.09.2024, with the mandate, inter alia, to identify such laws which are no 
longer needed or relevant and can be repealed.

(a) the details of funds sanctioned, released and utilised under the Bulk Drug Park Scheme for 
Himachal Pradesh since its inception, year-wise;  
(b) whether the Government has observed any gap between the release of funds and their actual 
utilisation during implementation of the said project, if so, the details thereof;  
(c) the milestones and timelines prescribed for creation of common infrastructure facilities under 
the said project along with the present status of their implementation;  
(d) whether any review has been conducted by the Government to identify reasons for delays or 
slow progress, if so, the details thereof; and  
(e) the corrective measures taken to ensure timely completion and operationalisation of the 
project? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
(a): Department of Pharmaceuticals (DoP), Government of India has sanctioned an amount of ₹ 
1000 crore on 11.10.2022 for development of Bulk Drug Park in Haroli, District Una, Himachal 
Pradesh under the Scheme for ‘Promotion of Bulk Drug Parks’ and out of which an amount of ₹ 
225 crore has been released on 20.02.2023 . The State Government, has also sanctioned an 
amount of ₹118.46 crore and released an amount of ₹ 35.53 crore as state share in F.Y. 22-23

(b) : The funds released are being utilized in a phased manner in accordance with approved

Utilization is linked with the execution of infrastructure components. 
 
(c) : Major common infrastructure facilities under implementation include site development, 
water supply system, power infrastructure, Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) with Zero 
Liquid Discharge (ZLD), steam generation system, warehouse, centre  of excellence, solvent 
recovery system, emergency response centre and solid waste management facilities. 
Present status is as under: 
 
i. About 20% work of Phase-I site development has been completed. 
ii. Approximately 98% of water supply and groundwater recharge works for 15 
MLD capacity have been completed. 
iii. 20 MVA power infrastructure required for the construction phase has been 
completed by HPSEBL.  
iv. Tenders for CETP with ZLD (₹273 crore) and Steam Generation System (₹300 
crore) are released. 
v. Procurement process for other critical utilities is underway. 
 
On the basis of representations received from the State Governments concerned, the 
status of projects, the level of fund utilisation and the anticipated completion of projects in 
FY2026–27, the tenure of the scheme has been extended up to FY2026-27.  
 
(d) and (e) : Yes Sir, t he review of the progress of the Bulk Drug Park being developed in 
Himachal Pradesh is regularly carried out by the Scheme Steering Committee of the scheme for 
“Promotion of Bulk Drug Park”, Secretary and Joint Secretary in the Department of 
Pharmaceuticals and by  High Powered Committee headed by Hon’ble Minister of Industries, 
Himachal Pradesh. Primary reasons affecting delay is the grant of Environmental Clearance 
which has been granted on 25.09.2025, procedural requirement for permission for felling of trees 
and bids for procurement. The State Government and implementing agencies are closely 
monitoring project execution and expediting statutory clearances, tendering and award of 
contracts for critical infrastructure components. Following receipt of Environmental Clearance, 
project acti vities have gained momentum, and multiple infrastructure packages are under 
implementation or advanced stages of procurement to ensure timely completion and 
operationalization of the park.

SAKSHAM ANGANWADI IN CHHATTISGARH  
  
2234. SHRI SANTOSH PANDEY:  
  
 Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
  
(a)  the current status of implementation of the Saksham Anganwadi Scheme and the number 
of Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) upgraded in Chhattisgarh, district -wise till July 2026; 
  
(b)  the key parameters and focus areas taken into consideration for transforming regular AWCs 
in to Saksham Anganwadis; 
  
(c)  the total amount of funds allocated for the upgradation of Anganwadis in Chhattisgarh, 
district-wise; and 
  
(d)  whether the Government faced any administration or infrastructural challenges during the 
upgradation process and if so, the details of the remedial measures and corrective steps 
taken to address them? 
  
 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (d) In the 15 th Finance Commission, components of nutritional support for children below 
the age of 6 years, pregnant women and lactating mothers, Adolescent Girls (14 – 18 years); Early 
Childhood Care and Education [3-6 years]; Anganwadi infrastructure including modern, upgraded 
Saksham Anganwadi, Poshan Abhiyaan and Scheme for Adolescent Girls were reorganised under 
Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0.  
Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, a package of six services i.e Supplementary 
Nutrition (SNP), Pre-school Non-formal Education, Nutrition & Health Education, Immunization, 
Health Check -up, and Referral Services are provided to the eligible be neficiaries through 
Anganwadi Centres across the country including State of Chhattisgarh. Three of the six services, 
viz., Immunization, Health check -up and Referral Services are related to health and are provided 
through National Health Mission (NHM) & Public Health Infrastructure. These ser vices are 
provided to the eligible registered beneficiaries i.e children up to the age of 6 years, Pregnant 

Women and Lactating Mothers across the country and Adolescent Girls in the age group of 14 to 
18 years in Aspirational Districts of States and all districts of North Eastern States.  
The district wise information on beneficiaries, supplementary nutrition and other parameters 
across the country including State of Chhattisgarh is available on the Poshan Tracker public 
dashboard at the link: https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics.  
Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, two lakh Anganwadi Centres  (AWCs) 
located in Government buildings have been sanctioned for upgradation as Saksham Anganwadis 
for delivery of improved nutrition and for Early Childhood Care and Education in the 15th Finance 
Commission cycle. Saksham Anganwadis  are provided with infrastructure such as LED screens, 
water filtration system, Poshan Vatika, Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) material and 
Building as Learning Aid (BALA) paintings.  A total of 11,490 AWCs have been approved for 
upgradation as S aksham Anganwadi in the State of Chhattisgarh and funds amounting to Rs. 
2,067.50 Lakh has been released for the same. The district wise details of AWCs approved for 
upgradation as Saksham Anganwadi centres in the State of Chhattisgarh is placed at Annexure.

(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (d) : Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, the ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital 
application has been rolled out as an ICT based governance tool for monitoring and tracking of all 
beneficiaries on various indicators. The number of children, pregnant women and lactating women 
registered in all the States and UTs including Chhattisgarh is available at Poshan Tracker public 
dashboard: https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics . 
To address network -related issues, such as low or no internet connectivity, the Poshan Tracker 
application provides offline functionality for conducting e -KYC and face matching under the 

Facial Recognition System (FRS) for the distribution of Take -Home Ration (THR). OTP for e -
KYC and Aadhar face matching has to be taken ONCE in entire life cycle of the beneficiary. It 
creates ease of living for the beneficiaries to avail the Anganwadi serv ices even when network or 
server issues are present. 
For further ease of receiving benefits of THR, Nominee Module has been introduced in the 
application for Pregnant Women, Lactating Mothers, and Adolescent Girls. If due to any reason, 
the registered beneficiary is unable to visit the Anganwadi Centre to re ceive THR through FRS, 
she can nominate a person on her behalf to receive her THR.  
As per Poshan Tracker data, e -KYC and face matching of the beneficiaries for THR distribution 
in the country has substantially increased in past one year from 70.82% in July 2025 to 97.87% in 
June 2026. State and UT wise details of e -KYC and Face matching (as of June 2026) is placed at 
Annexure I. 
Poshan Tracker application has been specifically designed to allow data entry in offline mode and 
the data can get synced within 5 days of entry. The frontline functionaries i.e. Anganwadi Workers, 
Block Coordinators and Supervisors are equipped with smart phones to enter the data of services 
at Anganwadi Centres and programme monitoring in the field.   
To address technical issues , Ministry of Women and Child Development (MoWCD) provides 
continuous training and handholding support to Anganwadi Workers for effective use of the 
Poshan Tracker application through the following mechanisms:  
• Learning Videos and awareness documents: In the Resource section of the Poshan Tracker 
application, learning videos and awareness documents are available for Anganwadi 
Workers which can be accessed by them at any point of time for effective delivery of the ir 
routine tasks. 
  
• Under the Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi (PBPB) initiative, the MoWCD is imparting training to 
all the officials and field functionaries in the States and UTs through a cascading model of 
training, wherein Master Trainers (District Officers, Block Coordinators and Supervisors) 
are trained and the master trainers further train all Anganwadi Workers in the field. 
Training is imparted on different modules of Poshan Tracker, viz. Facial Recognition 
System (FRS), Geo -Tagging, Home Visit Scheduler etc. Block and District coordinators 
provide on-ground handholding support to AWWs and supervisors for effective usage of 
the Poshan Tracker Application and resolution of technical glitches.  
  
• Daily Virtual Classroom Sessions: Digital India Corporation (DIC) organises virtual 
classroom sessions every day (Monday to Friday) from 3 pm to 4 pm, in which Anganwadi 
Workers may join to raise operational queries and receive real-time clarifications on use of 

the application. Further, training sessions from 4:15 PM to 5:15 PM for State officials 
(supervisor and above level) are organized to resolve implementation -related issues, 
disseminate updates, and provide training on newly introduced functionalities and 
enhancements in the Poshan Tracker application.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 2236
ANSWERED ON - 31/07/2026
REGULATION OF IMMIGRATION AGENTS
2236.  SHRI PUTTA MAHESH KUMAR
  SHRI MAGUNTA SREENIVASULU REDDY
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:-
(a) whether the Government is aware of the growing incidents of fake  
immigration agents and fraudulent overseas job/visa consultants cheating 
Indian citizens across the country, including Andhra Pradesh, if so, the  
details thereof;
(b) the details of the number of complaints received and cases registered 
against such agents, State/UT-wise, during the last three years, year-wise;
(c)  the  steps  taken  to  identify,  blacklist  and  prosecute  unauthorised 
agents, including action taken under the Emigration Act and coordination 
with State Police and other agencies; and
(d) whether the Government has undertaken any steps to strengthen  
public awareness, grievance redressal and prevention mechanisms for  
protecting emigrant workers, if so, the details thereof?

2
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)
(a to d) Recruitment Agencies (RA) in India for engaging in the recruitment 
business for overseas employment are regulated as per the provisions  
under The Emigration Act, 1983 and Rules thereunder. As per Section 10  
of  the Emigration Act, 1983, no person or agency can function as RA  
without a valid Registration Certificate (RC) issued by the Registering  
Authority,  i.e.,  Protector  General  of  Emigrants  (PGE).  Mandatory  
registration  of  RA  is  aimed  at  curbing  fraud  and  exploitation  of  
prospective Indian emigrants seeking overseas employment. 
The RC holders are required to comply with the provisions under the  
Emigration  Act,  1983,  and  the  terms  and  conditions  of  Registration  
Certificate prescribed in Section 10 of The Emigration Rules, 1983, which 
are focussed on safeguarding the interests of  emigrant workers. The  
Emigration Act/Rules, 1983 also provide for punitive actions against the  
registered RAs for violation of the provisions thereunder. 
Issuance of RC is done through eMigrate Portal (https://emigrate.gov.in)  
only which is maintained by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). List of  

3
all the registered RAs in India is publicly available on the eMigrate portal. 
List of unregistered agents against whom complaints were received, has  
also been published on the eMigrate portal to caution the prospective  
emigrants. As on date a total of 3,505 such unregistered agents have been 
notified on the eMigrate portal.
Instances  of  unauthorized  agents  involved  in  fraudulent  recruitment  
activities and cheating Indian citizens is taken into cognizance when such 
incidents are brought to the attention of the GOI. As and when complaints 
of illegal recruitment activities by unauthorized agents, including those  
from the State of  Andhra Pradesh, are received in the MEA, they are  
referred to the State/UT police for investigation and prosecution under the 
relevant  provisions  of  the  Bharatiya  Nyaya  Sanhita  (BNS)  and  other  
legislations in place. Data of complaints of illegal recruitment activities  
received from the States/UTs, including those from Andhra Pradesh, and  
action  taken  against  them  during  the  last  three  years  are  given  in  
Annexure-I. Data of complaints against unauthorized agent registered on  
eMigrate portal is given in Annexure-II.
Advisories are issued through the eMigrate portal, social media handles,  
and other modes about the perils of fake job rackets and ways to prevent 

4
illegal emigration through unauthorised RAs. The MEA, through the 17  
Protector of  Emigrants (POE) Offices across India, including the POE  
Office in Andhra Pradesh, also carries out awareness campaign on safe  
and  legal  mobility  by  conducting  workshops,  training/information  
sessions, digital campaigns for media groups, police officials and law  
enforcement agencies, local administration, and general public. MEA also 
coordinates  with  the  State  Nodal  agencies  on  the  issues  of  illegal  
recruitment activities by fake agencies. 
To address grievances of  Indian workers employed abroad, there are  
established  channels  to  enable  them  to  reach  out  to  the  Indian  
Missions/Posts  for  assistance.  They  can  contact  the  Missions/Posts  
through walk-in, email, multilingual 24x7 emergency numbers, WhatsApp  
number, grievance redressal portal like MADAD/CPGRAMS/eMigrate, and  
social media.  Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendras have been set up in  
key locations including New Delhi, Dubai, Jeddah, Kuala Lumpur, London  
and Riyadh to provide guidance and counselling to Indian workers. Indian 
Missions/Posts regularly organize Open Houses and Consular Camps in  
different cities to extend consular services and address any grievances.  
There are dedicated Labour Wings in the Indian Missions/Posts in most of 
the Gulf  countries which pro-actively take up grievances of  emigrant  

5
workers with the concerned FE, inspect the work place of the aggrieved  
worker  and  also  take  up,  where  required,  with  the  local  Labour  
Department and other host country authorities.   

6

A V AILABILITYOF ESSENTIAL MEDICINES IN GOVERNMENT HEALTHCARE
INSTITUTIONS
2237. SHRI MALAIYARASAN D:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the current status of availability of essential medicines and diagnostic facilities in Government
healthcare institutions in rural areas of Tamil Nadu, including Primary Health Centres (PHCs),
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) and district hospitals, district-wise including Kallakurichi
Parliamentary Constituency;
(b) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under various Central health schemes for
procurement of essential medicines strengthening of laboratories and improving diagnostic
services in rural Tamil Nadu during the last five years;
(c) whether the Government has assessed shortages, stock-outs or gaps in the availability of essential
medicines, medical supplies and diagnostic facilities in rural healthcare centres of the said State
and if so, the details threreof; and
(d) the steps being taken by the Union Government to ensure uninterrupted availability of affordable
medicines, essential diagnostics and quality healthcare services for rural populations, particularly
in remote and underserved areas of the said State?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) & (b): ‘Public Health’ and ‘Hospital’ are State subject and the responsibility for strengthening
of healthcare system including availability of essential medicines and diagnostic facilities in
Government healthcare institutions lies with respective State/UT Governments.
Under National Health Mission (NHM), financial and technical support is provided to
States/UTs to strengthen their healthcare system based on proposals received from States/UTs in their
Programme Implementation Plan (PIP) within their resource envelope.
Each year, PIP is formulated by every State/ UT based on district and State-level
planning processes, encompassing all activities and expenditures under NHM. State-wise fund
allocation can be accessed at:
https://nhm.gov.in/index1.php?lang=1&level=1&sublinkid=1377&lid=744

As per the information provided by the State Government of Tamil Nadu, the drugs
were categorized in to Essential Drug List (EDL) and Speciality Drug List (SDL) wherein 408 EDL
and 400 SDL are available in Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation (TNMSC) warehouses.
Under Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) component of Pradhan Mantri – Ayushman
Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) for the State of Tamil Nadu, Administrative
approvals have been accorded to the State for five years (i.e. FY 2021-22 to 2025-26) for an amount
of Rs.74.44 Cr. for construction and strengthening of 38 Integrated Public Health Labs (IPHLs) to
strengthen diagnostic infrastructure by enhancing access to quality essential diagnostic services.
Under Fifteenth Finance Commission (FC-XV) for the State of Tamil Nadu, Rs.301.07
Cr. has been approved from FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26 for strengthening of Block Public Health
Unit (BPHU) and Rs.301.07 Cr. has been released during the scheme period for establishment and
strengthening of 386 BPHU, to strengthen disease surveillance and provide diagnostic support.
(c) and (d): As per the information provided by the State Government of Tamil Nadu, there is no
shortage/stock-outs of drugs identified so far. Also, action is being taken to include certain drugs in
the EDL. Under Integrated Essential Laboratory Services (IELS) periodic gap analysis of essential
diagnostic investigations is carried out to assess the availability of diagnostic services across
healthcare facilities as well as Stock availability and utilisation are continuously monitored through
Drug Distribution and Management System (DDMS) Portal.
Further, Government of India supports the States in terms of drugs and diagnostics
services through State PIP proposals under Free Drugs Services Initiative and Free Diagnostic
Services Initiative every year.

2238. SHRI BALWANTBASWANTWANKHADE
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to State:
(a) the details of projects affected by the 2025 funding cuts under USAID/United States
President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) support towards HIV/AIDS prevention
in the country, State/UT-wise and project-wise;
(b) the estimated number of beneficiaries affected under such projects, including key
populations such as adolescents, transgender persons and people suffering with HIV ,State/UT-
wise and;
(c) the steps taken/proposed to be taken by the Union Government to sustain beneficiary
support provided under such projects, including Project (ACCELERATE) after the reduction or
withdrawal of external support?;
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (c) The National AIDS Control Programme is a fully domestic funded Central Sector
Scheme with around 5% contribution through the Global Fund Grant for HIV/AIDS. The
Government of India provides free prevention, testing and treatment services under the National
AIDS and STD Control Programme.
NACO has not received any funding support from USAID/PEPFAR. The funding cuts in the
USAID/PEPFAR support towards HIV/AIDS prevention in the country has not impacted service
provision for prevention, testing and treatment to High Risk Populations, at-risk populations and
People living with HIV under the National AIDS and STD Control Programme.
The National AIDS and STD Control Programme collaborates with international organisations,
bilateral and multilateral partner agencies including erstwhile USAID in technical areas
including sharing of best practices and innovations, training and capacity building for improving
HIV management cascade to meet India’s SDG commitments.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2240
TO BE ANSWERED ON 31.07.2026
SHORTAGE OF MEDICAL STAFF IN HOSPITALS
†2240. SHRI BRIJENDRA SINGH OLA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that thousands of posts of doctors, specialists, physicians, nurses and
paramedical staff are still lying vacant in many Government hospitals and health centres in
the country, due to which patients are unable to get timely treatment;
(b) if so, the details of the vacant posts at present, category-wise and State/UT-wise including
Rajasthan, along with the number of appointments made to these posts during the last three
years;
(c) whether the Government has taken note that due to the shortage of medicines, diagnostic
facilities, ICU beds and medical equipment in several Government hospitals, patients are
being forced to resort to private hospitals, if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the concrete steps taken by the Government to rectify or remove these deficiencies and to
ensure quality and timely healthcare services in all Government hospitals along with the
timeline fixed for the same?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (d): Health is a State subject. The primary responsibility of strengthening public
healthcare system, including vacant posts lies with the respective State/UT Governments. The
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to the
States/UTs to strengthen the public healthcare system in rural areas based on the proposals
received in the form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health
Mission. Government of India provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of
Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources. States/ UTs to ensure availability of
HR by creating adequate number of regular posts as per the Indian Public Health Standards
(IPHS) in the long run and using NHM posts in the short to medium term to fill critical gaps.

The NHM supplements the regular human resources by filling up the gaps in human
resources in secondary and primary care facilities (District Hospital and below) as per IPHS.
The details of doctors, specialists, physicians, nurses and paramedical staff in
Government hospitals and health centres across the country and their vacancies State/UT-
wise including Rajasthan can be accessed at the following link of HDI 2023-24:
https://www.mohfw-dohfw.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/05/57202cf30629539e4d0fb0a2f700ac
62.pdf
To ensure availability of essential drugs and reduce the Out-of-Pocket Expenditure
(OOPE) of the patients visiting the public health facilities, Government has rolled out the
Free Drugs Service Initiative (FDSI) under National Health Mission. This includes financial
support to States/UTs for 113 drugs at Sub Health Centre level, 179 at Primary Health Centre
level, 301 at Community Health Centre level, 318 at Sub District Hospital level and 381
drugs at district Hospitals.
This Ministry supports ‘Free Diagnostics Service Initiative’ programme under NHM
with the aim to provide accessible and affordable pathological and radiological diagnostics
services closer to the community, which in turn reduces the Out-of-Pocket Expenditure
(OOPE). Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities
(14 tests at Sub Centers, 63 at Primary Health Centers, 97 at Community Health Centres, 111
test at Sub District Hospitals and 134 tests at District Hospitals).
Under NHM, following types of incentives and honorarium are provided to ensure
quality and timely healthcare services in all Government hospitals:
• Hard area allowances to specialist doctors for serving in rural and remote areas and
for their residential quarters so that they find it attractive to serve in public health facilities in
such areas.
• Honorarium to Gynecologists/ Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC) trained,
Pediatricians & Anesthetist/ Life Saving Anaesthesia Skills (LSAS) trained doctors is also
provided to increase availability of specialists for conducting Cesarean Sections in rural &
remote area.

• Incentives like special incentives for doctors, incentive for Auxiliary Nurse and
Midwife (ANM) for ensuring timely Antenatal Checkup (ANC) checkup and recording,
incentives for conducting Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health activities.
• States are also allowed to offer negotiable salary to attract specialist including
flexibility in strategies such as “You Quote We Pay”.
• Non-Monetary incentives such as preferential admission in post graduate courses for
staff serving in difficult areas and improving accommodation arrangement in rural areas have
also been introduced under NHM.
• Multi-skilling of doctors is supported under NHM to overcome the shortage of
specialists. Skill upgradation of existing HR is another major strategy under NRHM for
achieving improvement in health outcomes.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 31ST JULY,2026
REJECTION OF CLAIMS UNDER AB-PMJAY
2241. DR. KALANIDHI VEERASWAMY:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the impact of rejected claims
on beneficiaries seeking timely medical treatment under AB-PMJAY ,if so, the details thereof;
and
(b) the measures taken by the Government to reduce claim rejection rates, strengthen
grievance redressal mechanisms, improve transparency in claim processing and ensure that
eligible beneficiaries receive timely healthcare benefits under the Scheme?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) and (b): Under Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), all
claims submitted by empanelled hospitals are adjudicated in accordance with Standard
Treatment Guidelines, Health Benefit Package protocols, and the prescribed claims
adjudication manual.
Under the scheme, claim adjudication is continuously monitored by National Health
Authority (NHA) through a robust IT-enabled Transaction Management System. Regular
analysis of claim processing trends, including rejected claims, is undertaken to identify
operational issues, improve claim adjudication quality, and facilitate corrective measures in
coordination with the States/UTs.
To ensure that eligible claims are not rejected without adequate scrutiny, a structured
multi-level claim adjudication and review process is followed under AB-PMJAY .Before a
claim is finally rejected, it is examined at multiple levels by designated medical and
administrative authorities in accordance with the prescribed claim adjudication processes. In
addition, a dedicated review committee has been established wherein empanelled hospitals
may submit requests for review of rejected or partially paid claims within 15 days from the
date of communication of the decision. Such requests are examined by a designated
committee before arriving at a final decision.

Further, NHA regularly engages with States/UTs through review meetings, capacity-building
initiatives, and monitoring mechanisms to improve the quality and timelines of claim
processing.
In cases of any irregularities in availing treatment by an empanelled hospital, beneficiaries
can register their grievances through the Centralized Grievance Redressal Management
System or the 24×7 toll-free helpline (14555), Ayushman App, and Ayushman Sarathi
(WhatsApp chatbot). Under AB-PMJAY ,such grievances are monitored through a three-tier
grievance redressal mechanism at the District, State and National level. At each level,
designated nodal officers and Grievance Redressal Committees are in place to examine and
resolve the grievances, thereby strengthening accountability and facilitating effective
implementation of the Scheme.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF PHARMACEUTICALS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2242 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 31st JULY 2026 
  
Jan Aushadhi Kendras in Uttar Pradesh  
 
†2242. Shri Anoop Pradhan Valmiki: 
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the number of Jan Aushadhi Kendra (JAKs) sanctioned/functional operational in Hathras 
district of Uttar Pradesh till date;  
(b) whether the Government is aware that a few JAKs have been closed due to problems like 
below optimal sales, lesser prescription of generic medicines by the doctors and non -supply 
of medicines in a timely manner in the said district, if so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether the Government has conducted any investigation/review in this regard, if so, the 
details thereof; and  
(d) the steps being taken by the Government for operating JAKs in an effective manner 
creating awareness regarding generic medicines and ensuring regular supply of medicines? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS                                   
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a): Under Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana, a total of 4 ,226 Jan Aushadhi 
Kendras (JAKs) have been opened in the State of Uttar Pradesh as on 30.06.2026, of which 
17 JAKs have been opened in the Hathras district.   
 
(b): Yes Sir. In the Hathras district of Uttar Pradesh, 02 Jan Aushadhi Kendras have become 
non-operational till 30.06.2026.  
 
(c): The Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI) , the implementing 
agency of the scheme  continuously monitor s the functioning of Jan Aushadhi Kendras  
through an IT-enabled monitoring system, regular review of sales and stock positions.  
 
Further, the State Level Marketing Officer of PMBI, establishes contact with JAKs 
whose sales are low with a view to help revive sales. PMBI handholds JAKs and organises 
workshops, peer learning from successful JAK owners and meeting with doctors from the 
local area for JAKs performing less well.  

(d): The Government has taken several measures to ensure the effective functioning of Jan 
Aushadhi Kendras  creating awareness regarding generic medicines and ensuring regular 
supply of medicines. Details are as under:-  
  
In order t o promote acceptability and to increase sale of medicines supplied through 
JAKs, targeted awareness campaigns about the benefits of Janaushadhi medicines are 
conducted on a regular basis:  
i. Awareness campaigns: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India 
(PMBI), conducts awareness campaigns in coordination with bodies and platforms 
such as the Central Bureau of Communication, PIB, MyGov and MY Bharat, in 
various modes such as print, t elevision, radio, social media platforms, outdoor 
hoardings, community engagement, etc.  
ii. Interactive messages/calls: Outreach and citizen engagement are also pursued through 
WhatsApp chatbot and outbound calls to inform citizens regarding the quality of 
Janaushadhi products and the large savings that accrue from purchase of the same from 
nearest JAK.  
iii. Jan Aushadhi Week: Jan Aushadhi Week is celebrated every year in the first week of 
March during which special campaigns such as public rallies, health camps, seminars 
in pharmacy colleges, children engagement programmes, etc. are conducted across the 
nation to educate citizens, healthcare professionals and other stakeholders about the 
benefits of Janaushadhi generic medicines. 
iv. Messages from eminent persons: Audio/video messages from well -known persons 
such as public representatives and eminent doctors are disseminated on social media 
platforms to highlight the benefits of Janaushadhi medicines and dispel myths 
associated with respect to their quality.  
v. Public engagement programme in rural areas: To educate citizens in local 
languages/dialects, publicity is also done through health camps, nukkad -natak, 
audiovisual display at Common Service Centres and public engagement workshops in 
association with local JAKs in rural areas. 
In order to address any supply gaps and ensure smooth supply and availability of 
products at JAKs, the following measures are in place: 
 
(i) Since September 2024, stocking by JAKs of 200 commonly used medicines, 
consisting of the 100 top-selling medicines in the scheme product basket and 100 fast-
selling medicines in the market, has been incentivised, under which JAK owners are 
eligible for mon thly incentive based on the stocks that they maintain for these 
medicines.  
(ii) An end -to-end information -technology-enabled supply chain system is in place to 
connect a robust supply chain system consisting of five warehouses and a growing 
network of distributors across the country, currently numbering 42.  
(iii)In addition, with a view to ensure availability of commonly used products, 400 fast -
moving products are monitored regularly by Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices 
Bureau of India (PMBI), the scheme implementing agency, and demand for the same 
is estimated on a continuous basis. Further, steps have been taken to digitise the 
estimation method to augment the procurement process.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 31.07.2026
UTILIZATION OF FUND UNDER PM-ABHIM
2243. SHRI BRIJMOHAN AGRAWAL:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
a) the total amount of funds allocated and utilized under the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman
Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) during 2025–26 and the number
of Critical Care Blocks (CCBs) currently operational nationwide;
b) the reasons for the persistent gap between physical infrastructure completion and the
recruitment of specialized personnel under the National Health Mission (NHM)
protocols;
c) the status of vacant specialist positions (anesthesiologists, critical care nurses) in
Chhattisgarh and its impact on service delivery for tribal populations, district wise;
and
d) the details of any mandatory "Readiness Certification" or "Recruitment-Integrated"
approval policies initiated to ensure new facilities are staffed and functional
immediately upon completion, including specific audit timelines for the current
fiscal year?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (d): Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) is a
Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) with certain Central Sector (CS) components, has been
implemented to strengthen India's public health system through reforms that integrate health
service delivery, public health action and health research, thereby enhancing the capacity of
public health systems to effectively respond to pandemics and other public health
emergencies. The State/UT-wise details of Central Release and Expenditure under PM-
ABHIM for FY 2025-26 are placed at Annexure-I. Further, the State/UT-wise details of
Critical Care Blocks (CCBs) approved, Work Under Progress and Functional, as reported by
the State/UTs, are placed at Annexure-II.
Under National Health Mission (NHM), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
provides technical and financial support to the States/UTs for strengthening public healthcare

infrastructure and ensuring the availability of adequate human resources to improve access to
quality healthcare, particularly for underserved and marginalized populations in rural areas.
Such support is provided based on the proposals submitted by the States/UTs in their
Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs), which are approved by the Government of India in
the form of Records of Proceedings (RoPs), subject to NHM norms and the availability of
resources. As health is a State subject, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare works
closely with the States/UTs to facilitate timely recruitment and deployment of healthcare
personnel in newly created health facilities. To improve the availability and retention of
skilled human resources, States/UTs are supported in implementing measures such as hard
area allowances, residential accommodation, performance-based incentives, and multi-
skilling of existing healthcare personnel, including training of General Medical Officers in
Emergency Obstetric Care and Life-Saving Anesthesia Skills, to strengthen service delivery
in rural and remote areas.
As per Health Dynamics of India (HDI) 2023-24, details of vacant specialist positions
(anesthesiologists, staff nurses etc.) in tribal areas of the country, including Chhattisgarh, may
be seen at the following link:
https://www.mohfw-dohfw.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/05/57202cf30629539e4d0fb0a2f700ac62.pdf.
Monitoring under the National Health Mission (NHM) and PM-ABHIM is carried out
through a robust, multi-layered framework that includes review of State-wise Key
Deliverables against approved targets during NPCC meetings with all States/UTs, regular
assessment of performance through the Output–Outcome Monitoring Framework (OOMF).
In addition, annual Common Review Missions (CRMs) provide independent, on-ground
assessments of programme implementation, health system strengthening, and progress on key
indicators, enabling identification of gaps, course correction, and strengthening of
accountability at State and District levels.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE 
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2244 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 31ST JULY, 2026 
 
DECORUM IN COURTROOM 
 
2244. SHRI SURESH KUMAR SHETKAR:  
 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether training or sensitisation programmes are conducted for advocates regarding 
courtroom behaviour, if so, the details thereof and the effectiveness of such initiatives;  
(b) whether adequate security arrangements are in place in court premises to prevent 
disruptions, if so, the details thereof and gaps identified;  
(c) whether technological interventions such as CCTV monitoring are being used to ensure 
courtroom discipline, if so, the details thereof and coverage across courts;  
(d) whether complaints regarding unruly behaviour or intimidation in courtrooms have been 
received, if so, the details thereof and the actions taken to address such concerns; and  
(e) whether the Government has consulted the Bar Council of India to enforce professional 
conduct standards, if so, the details thereof and compliance measures thereon? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW 
AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a) to (e): Chapter II of Part VI of the Bar Council of India Rules (Standards of Professional 
Conduct and Etiquette) lays down the standards of professional conduct to be observed by 
Advocates. The Rules, inter alia, require every advocate to maintain a respectful at titude 
towards the Court, conduct himself/herself with dignity and propriety, use dignified language, 
and uphold the honour and dignity of the judicial institution. 
 
The Advocates Act, 1961 provides a statutory mechanism for enforcement of 
professional conduct and discipline of advocates. Sections 35 and 36 of the Act empower the 
State Bar Councils and the Bar Council of India, respectively, to initiate disciplinary 
proceedings and impose appropriate penalties in cases of professional or other misconduct. The 
standards of professional conduct and etiquette are prescribed under Chapter II of Part VI of 
the Bar Council of India Rules, and compliance thereof is enforced th rough the disciplinary 
framework provided under the Act.  
 
The incidences involving breach of decorum in courtroom can also be dealt under the 
Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, which defines and limits the powers of certain courts in 
punishing contempt of courts and regulates their procedure in relation thereto. The A ct inter 

2 
 
alia addresses the acts of publication (whether by words, spoken or written, or by signs, or by 
visible representations, or otherwise) of any matter or the doing of any other act whatsoever 
which— (i) scandalises or tends to scandalise, or lowers or tends to lower the authority of, any 
court; or (ii) prejudices, or interferes or tends to interfere with, the due course of any judicial 
proceeding; or (iii) interferes or tends to interfere with, or obstructs or tends to obstruct, the 
administration of justice in any other manner. 
 
The Central Government does not maintain a centralized database for tracking 
complaints regarding unruly behaviour or intimidation in courtrooms. ‘Police’ and ‘Public 
Order’ are State subjects under the Constitution. The responsibility to provide security to 
institutions including courts lies primarily with the State Governments. Government deploys 
Central Armed Police Forces to aid and assist State Governments to maintain law and order, 
and extends financial assistance to them to modernize and build capacity of their police forces.  
 
The Supreme Court of India, in its order dated 11.08.2023 in the Writ Petition 
(Criminal) No. 99 of 2015 ( Pradyuman Bisht versus Union of India & others ), while laying 
down guidelines regarding security measures in the courts, directed that the schematics of 
CCTV camera installation will have to be laid down on a district -wise basis where the 
respective State Governments should provide the requisite funds  for the execution of such a 
plan in a timely manner. The Court further directed that upon the finalisat ion of the security 
plan, the High Courts may entrust the responsibility of installation and maintenance of the 
CCTV cameras with the concerned District and Sessions Judges for a more realistic analysis 
of local requirements.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
 DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS  
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2245 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 31.07.2026 
 
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samruddhi Kendras 
 
2245 Shri Saumitra Khan: 
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samruddhi Kendras (PMKSKs) converted 
from existing fertilizer retail outlets across the country, State-wise including West 
Bengal; 
(b) the total financial outlay, allocation and actual expenditure incurred on the rebranding 
and conversion of retail fertilizer shops into PMKSKs especially in Bankura District of 
West Bengal during the last three financial years; 
(c) whether any independent evaluation has been conducted to assess that PMKSKs 
have improved farmers’ access to fertilizers, seeds, soil testing services and agri-input 
advisories, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether instances of fertilizer shortages, delayed supply or uneven distribution have 
been reported in PMKSKs especially in West Bengal during the last three years, if so, 
the details thereof; and 
(e) the number of PMKSKs equipped with functional soil testing facilities and trained 
personnel to provide scientific advisories? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
 (SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a)  Out of a total 2,89,605 retailer across the country having active  Point of Sales (PoS), 
as on 30.07.2026, 1,54,706 have been developed into PMKSKs. Out of these 12,088 
PMKSKs are in West Bengal. The State-wise list of PMKSKs, including those in West 
Bengal, is enclosed at Annexure A.  
(b) There is no separate financial allocation/outlay by the Government for the 
conversion of retail shops into PMKSKs. However, as per Department of Fertilizers’ 
communication dated 15.11.2022, it has been decided that the cost towards conversion of 
existing village/block/sub district/ taluk and district level fertilizer retail shops into "Pradhan 
Mantri Kisan Samridhi Kendra" (PMKSK) is to be met by the fertilizer companies from the 
retailer margin/incentives of Rs. 50/MT allowed for acknowledging the receipt of fertilizer 
through fertilizer monitoring system. 

(c) No Sir. No such independent evaluation has been conducted to assess whether 
PMKSKs have improved farmers' access to fertilizers, seeds, soil testing services, and agri-
input advisories.  
(d) Agriculture Department of West Bengal has informed that there is no shortages, 
delayed supply or uneven distribution of fertilizers in West Bengal. 
In addition to this, following Steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate supply of fertilizers across the States/UTs, including the State of West 
Bengal: 
i. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis 
of requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
ii. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
iii. The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizer is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well 
in advance to ensure timely availability.  
iv. The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers 
and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
v. Regularly coordinate with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient rakes, 
priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district level is done by the concerned State 
government. 
Accordingly, the availability of fertilizers has remained adequate across the 
States/UTs, including the State of West Bengal, in the last three years (i.e. in FYs 2023-24, 
2024-25 and 2025-26). The information regarding requirement, availability, sales and 
closing stocks of fertilizers in the States/UTs during the said period is placed at Annexure 
B. 
(e)  As on 30.07.2026, a total of 47,206 PMKSKs across the country have been 
equipped with soil and water testing facilities. 
Fertilizer companies like IFFCO, KRIBHCO, CIL, RCF, MATIX, etc. have informed 
that Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samruddhi Kendras (PMKSKs) provide services to improve 
farmers' access to soil testing and scientific advisory services. Many PMKSKs have also 
been equipped with soil testing facilities and trained personnel to support these services. 
Through PMKSKs, trained staff collect soil samples from farmers and send them to soil 
testing laboratories, including static and mobile laboratories, for testing. Based on the test 
results, farmers are provided with soil test reports and scientific advice on the balanced use 
of fertilizers and crop nutrient management. 

PMKSKs also serve as centres for farmer awareness and training. Farmer meetings, 
soil health awareness programmes, PM PRANAM Sangoshthis, and programmes 
organised during PM-KISAN instalment distribution are regularly conducted through 
PMKSKs. During these programmes, agricultural experts provide guidance on soil health, 
balanced fertilizer use, crop nutrition, and improved farming practices. Awareness 
materials, nutrient deficiency charts, and other information are also displayed at PMKSKs 
to help farmers understand the importance of soil testing and proper nutrient management.
