UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2246
TO BE ANSWERED ON 31ST JULY,2026
HEALTH INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR NEWBORN
2246. SHRI MADDILA GURUMOORTHY:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware that except for corporate insurance policies provided by
employers, neither private insurance companies nor Central/State health schemes provide
comprehensive medical coverage for newborns from day one, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether it is a fact that most private insurers offer neonatal coverage only under special
riders or with long waiting periods and inadequate sub-limits, leaving families financially
burdened, if so the details thereof;
(c) whether the Government proposes to mandate universal health insurance coverage for
newborns from birth under Ayushman Bharat or any national scheme; and
(d) if so, the timeline for implementation thereof and if not, the reasons for failing to address
the growing disparity between average household income and escalating neonatal healthcare
costs in the country?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (d): As per Department of Financial Services, insurers offer a range of health insurance
products catering to health insurance needs of the newborns. While some products provide
such coverage with sub-limits and/or waiting periods, others offer coverage from the first day
of birth without any sub-limits or waiting periods. The premium varies depending on the extent
of coverage and benefits offered. Accordingly, policyholders may choose a product based on
their coverage requirements and affordability.
Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana provides coverage for 1,961
treatment procedures across 27 medical specialities, including speciality for Neonatal Care
comprising 13 procedures covering basic, critical and advanced neonatal care etc. Newborns
are covered under the scheme from the day of birth as part of the beneficiary family, in
accordance with the scheme guidelines.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2247
TO BE ANSWERED ON 31-07-2026
KEY HEALTH INDICATORS
2247. SHRI SUNIL BOSE:
Will the Minister of HEALTH & FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the reasons for delays in the release of key health indicators, such as the
latest National Family Health Survey (NFHS) data and Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR)
updates, as of 2025;
(b) the steps being taken by the Government to ensure timely and transparent
dissemination of critical health data to support evidence-based policymaking and public
health initiatives; and
(c) the details of the impact of the aforementioned delays on initiatives such as the
Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, Adolescent Health Plus Nutrition (RMNCAH+N)
strategy?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL)
(a) to (c) The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoH&FW) conducts an integrated
survey namely National Family Health Survey (NFHS). The survey provides data on health
and family welfare and associated domains like characteristics of the population; fertility and
fertility preferences; family planning; maternal and child health; nutrition; morbidity and
healthcare; women’s empowerment, etc. The National and State/UT Fact Sheets of sixth
round of NFHS (2023-24) were released on 29.05.2026. The Fact Sheets are available in the
public domain and can be accessed at:
https://www.nfhsiips.in/nfhsuser/assets/National%20Family%20Health%20Survey%20(NFH
S-6)%202023-2024%20Fact%20Sheets.pdf
Sample Registration System (SRS) of Office of the Registrar General & Census
Commissioner of India is a large-scale demographic survey that provides estimates of various
fertility and mortality indicators at National and subnational levels. Maternal Mortality Ratio
(MMR) is one of the indicators which results from Sample Registration system (SRS). The
SRS is one of the world's largest demographic survey covering around 89 lakhs population

spread across 36 States/UTs in the country. The latest Sample Registration System (SRS)-
Special Bulletin on Maternal Mortality in India 2022-24 released in May 2026 by the
Registrar General of India. The latest publication is for the period 2022-24 and may be
accessed from the following link:
https://censusindia.gov.in/census.website/data/SRSMMB
The Ministry timely disseminates NFHS data by conducting regular follow-ups with the nodal
agency and regular meetings at higher levels to monitor progress and oversee intermediary
steps.
Under National Health Mission, Government of India, the child health, adolescent health, and
nutrition interventions are universally implemented and routinely monitored under the
RMNCAH+N strategy of the National Health Mission, irrespective of the timing of the
release of any report.

ESTABLISHMENT OF REGIONAL MEDICAL HUBS
2248. SHRI TEJASVI SURYA:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Scheme for supporting States in establishing five Regional Medical Hubs, as announced
in the Union Budget 2026–27 to strengthen India's healthcare ecosystem and promote medical value
travel, has been notified;
(b) if so, the details thereof including the guidelines and eligibility criteria for selection of States and if
not, the expected timeline for its notification;
(c) whether the Government has received any proposal from the State Government of Karnataka for
establishing one of the Regional Medical Hubs in the State, if so, the details thereof including its present
status; and
(d) the criteria and timeline fixed for the selection of States for establishing the five Regional Medical
Hubs along with the expected timeline for operationalising the selected hubs?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILYWELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (d): The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) has undertaken
extensive stakeholder consultations, including through a post-Budget webinar with domain experts,
concerned Ministries and Departments, healthcare institutions, industry associations, representatives of
the hospitality sector, multilateral organisations and other stakeholders. The implementation framework
is currently under consideration and no formal proposals have been invited from State Governments so
far.

RIGHT TO PRIMARY HEALTHCARE FOR REGISTERED PHARMACISTS
†2249. SHRI UJJWALRAMAN SINGH:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is considering granting registered pharmacists the right to
provide primary healthcare and to engage in limited practice;
(b) if so, the details and the timeframe thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (c): The Pharmacy Practice Regulations, 2015 regulate the practice of pharmacy by
registered pharmacists. The Regulations prescribe various duties and responsibilities for
registered pharmacists, inter alia, including dispensing medicines only against prescriptions
issued by Registered Medical Practitioners, providing practical training to student
pharmacists, maintaining patient records, ensuring patient confidentiality, promoting the
rational use of medicines, adhering to professional ethics, and counselling patients to ensure
the safe and effective use of medicines.
*****
